title: Appeal calls for attention
odia:
ନ ଲାଗିଲେ ସବୁବେଳେ
ଘର କି ଶୋଭେ
ନ ମାଠିଲେ ବୟସ ବେଳେ
ମନ କି ଲୋଭେ?
literal_meaning: Without continual effort, does the house look pleasing? Without polishing in one’s prime, is the heart attracted?
meaning_odia: ନିୟମିତ ଲାଗି ନରହିଲେ ଘର ଶୋଭା ପାଏ କି, ବୟସ ବେଳେ ମାଠିବା ନହେଲେ ମନ ଆକର୍ଷିତ ହୁଏ କି—ଦୁଇଟି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ମାଠିବାକୁ ଘଷିମାଜି ପରିଷ୍କାର ବା ପରିମାର୍ଜିତ କରିବାର ବ୍ୟାପକ ଅର୍ଥରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ଠିକ୍ କେଉଁ ଜିନିଷକୁ କିପରି ମାଠିବା କୁହାଯାଇଛି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସହ ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ପ୍ରୟାସର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଏହା ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ।
explanation: Both questions place work before appeal: sustained attention for the house, polishing or refinement in one’s prime. Our editorial reading connects a pleasing result with effort rather than assuming it arrives by itself. The second question leaves the thing being polished unstated, so this edition keeps that action broad.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone expects a project to remain inviting without regular attention. A colleague recalls the paired questions about effort and appeal.
cultural_context: The house gives the first question a concrete object. The second turns to attraction while leaving its object implicit. Repeating the negative condition and rhetorical question links the two without identifying a particular grooming or social practice.
